title: Recursive unfolding of the Gowers product
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, let $k \ge 0$, let $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ be a base point, and let $h_1, \ldots, h_{k+1} \in \{0,1\}^n$ be direction vectors. Then the order-$(k{+}1)$ Gowers product splits along its last direction as
\[
  \mathrm{GP}(f, k{+}1, x, h_1, \ldots, h_{k+1})
  = \mathrm{GP}(f, k, x, h_1, \ldots, h_k)
    \cdot \mathrm{GP}(f, k, x \oplus h_{k+1}, h_1, \ldots, h_k),
\]
where $x \oplus h_{k+1}$ denotes the componentwise XOR.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on {0,1}^n
x is a base point in {0,1}^n
replaced:
For any $f$, $k \ge 0$, $x$, and direction vectors $h_1,\ldots,h_{k+1}$, the
Gowers product unfolds as
\[
  \mathrm{GP}(f, k{+}1, x, h_1,\ldots,h_{k+1})
  = \mathrm{GP}(f, k, x, h_1,\ldots,h_k)
    \cdot \mathrm{GP}(f, k, x \oplus h_{k+1}, h_1,\ldots,h_k).
\]
